newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower but pares losses late.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower but pares losses late.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower but pared their losses amid late spillover strength from CBOT wheat, traders said.
"Chicago had technical and commercial buying late, and Kansas City was just a following market," a KCBT trader said.

Wheat opened lower after USDA's weekly wheat export sales report came in below trade expectations. USDA said net export sales during the week ended July 17 totaled 259,500 tonnes, below expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
KCBT wheat was also pressured at midsesion by hedging tied to an increase in farmer selling.
Traders said higher wheat prices in recent days have induced more farmers to sell their grain, prompting country elevators to put on extra hedges.
KCBT wheat settled 1/2 to two cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 1/2 cent at $3.67-1/4. Earlier, Sept had hit an intraday low at $3.64, down 3-3/4 cents on the day.
Traders said Cargill Investor Services was a featured buyer, picking up 1.7 million Sept. FIMAT bought 1.2 million Sept and 1.1 million Dec but also sold 1.5 million Sept.
